driver: second independent confirmation of the flicker, real content instead of flat colors
veredicto: mode 1 (4320x2160@90), leblon_vr180.mp4 via jack-in-wayland.sh + play360.sh: stable ~60fps decode/upload for the video (software decode, NVDEC hwaccel doesn't support width 4320>4096), but the user reports it STILL FLICKERS as if it were 60Hz -- same as with hmd-vk and flat colors (T020). Second independent confirmation: the flicker doesn't depend on content type, so it isn't a rendering artifact. Reinforces the hypothesis from docs/04-lab-90hz.md: the backlight strobe may be tied to something other than the refresh rate negotiated with the driver.

driver: check whether bright full-screen content gives a stronger signal than the power-on event
veredicto: hmd-vk native 1 (flat alternating colors) recorded with camera 15s@10fps, LED covered, pointed at the lens: average frame luma went from 237.78 to 120.24 with a total range of 114.95-237.78 (vs 6-10 in all the power-on/off tests). Visually confirmed in frame_00001 (saturated white) vs frame_00075 (light-blue/gray background) -- the camera DOES detect color/content changes with full-screen brightness. Doesn't resolve the 60/90Hz strobe (Nyquist limit, see note in NEXT-STEP.md), but confirms the camera channel is viable for verifying that content/color changes are present, provided the content is bright and the camera is properly aimed.

driver: rule out the wrong-mode hypothesis -- Windows uses this exact timing with no reported flicker, confirmed by CRU in docs/19
veredicto: hmd-vk native 0 (2880x1440@89.999, unmodified EDID timing, byte-identical to what was captured with CRU on Windows in docs/19): image present, alternating colors visible, BUT the user reports clear flicker -- same as T020/T021 with the supersampled 4320x2160 mode. Rules out the hypothesis that the supersampled (non-native) mode was the cause of the flicker: even with timing byte-identical to what Windows uses with no known flicker complaint, the flicker persists on Linux. Third independent confirmation of the flicker.

driver: confirm whether the flicker is a panel trait (would flicker the same on both OSes) or specific to how Linux negotiates the link
veredicto: Confirmed by the user on Windows: 60Hz FLICKERS, 90Hz does NOT flicker -- exactly the opposite of Linux (where 90Hz flickers, T020/T021/T023). Definitively rules out a physical panel/headset defect -- if it were one, it would flicker the same way on both OSes. Confirms it's a real behavior tied to the mode, specific to how Linux negotiates the link/backlight at 90Hz. Also confirmed that /sys/kernel/debug/dri/*/DP-1/dpcd doesn't exist for this connector (NVIDIA doesn't expose AUX/DPCD through the generic DRM helpers), and that USB capture could never have seen this to begin with (AUX/DPCD isn't a USB protocol). With no hardware DP analyzer, available software tools are exhausted.

driver: confirm left+right connect after resolving the -71 error from the cold reboot
veredicto: Post-reboot the headset's companion/USB2/USB3 devices weren't enumerating (error -71, cold boot). Resolved with a simple physical replug of the cable -- no port or orientation change this time, just disconnecting and reconnecting was enough. After that all 5 devices enumerated cleanly (USB2 hub, audio, companion, USB3 hub, HoloLens Sensors). Controllers: left connected on monado-service's first startup; right didn't appear in the initial summary but connected shortly after (Reading right controller config in the log) -- the summary is a snapshot taken before pairing finished, not an actual failure. Both confirmed via log after power-cycling both controllers.
